title: Annular Majorana mode in a superconducting topological insulator
authors: Shengshan Qin, Chi Wu, Lun-hui Hu, Tiantian Zhang, Jiangping Hu
abstract: When the surface states of a topological insulator becomes superconducting, topological superconductivity can be obtained, and each vortex on the surface can host one single Majorana zero-energy mode which is usually a wave packet decaying exponentially off the vortex core. Here, we predict stable Majorana zero-energy mode whose wave function is ring-shape, dubbed as annular Majorana mode, in the superconducting vortex in topological insulators respecting $3$-fold or $6$-fold rotational symmetry. Such topological insulators are featured with a single nonlinear Dirac cone located at $\barΓ$ or three linear Dirac cones at $\bar{\text{M}}$ in the surface Brillouin zone. The annular Majorana mode originates from the effective chiral $f$-wave superconductivity on the nonlinear Dirac cone in the former case and the interference of the effective chiral $p$-wave superconductivity on the three linear Dirac cones in the latter. In both cases, the annular Majorana mode is stabilized by the rotational symmetry and the winding number $3$ carried by the surface states. Candidate materials supporting the annular Majorana mode are predicted. Our work provides new insights into the topological superconductivity in superconducting topological insulators.
summary: This work theoretically predicts the existence of an annular Majorana mode within superconducting vortices hosted on topological insulators. The stability of this unique, ring-shaped zero-energy state is linked to specific crystalline symmetries and a total surface state winding number of three. It provides concrete predictions for candidate materials like $\text{ZrTi}_2$ where such exotic topological superconductivity can be realized.
main_problem: The paper predicts a novel, stable Majorana zero-energy mode characterized by a ring shape (annular) within superconducting vortices in topological insulators.
main_result: This annular Majorana mode is stabilized by the rotational symmetry and winding number 3 of the surface states, existing either from a nonlinear Dirac cone at $\bar{\Gamma}$ or three linear cones at $\bar{M}$.
method: The analysis involves solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian for superconducting vortices and performing symmetry analysis on the resulting bound states.
model_or_system: The system is a topological insulator surface state made superconducting, specifically requiring 3-fold or 6-fold rotational symmetry. The model considers two cases: a single nonlinear Dirac cone at $\bar{\Gamma}$ or three linear Dirac cones at $\bar{M}$.
key_observables: The primary observable is the real-space wave function profile, which is predicted to be ring-shaped (annular), contrasting with exponentially decaying modes.
important_parameters: Rotational symmetry ($3$-fold or $6$-fold); winding number of 3; superconducting gap $\Delta$; and momentum scattering terms ($	ilde{A}, 	ilde{B}$).
main_assumptions: The initial analysis assumes the adiabatically reachable condition where a specific coupling term ($	ilde{B}$) is zero, although stability is shown even when finite.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two physical conditions supporting the annular MZM and show the resulting ring-like wave function profile in real space for the nonlinear Dirac cone case.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by identifying the necessary symmetry conditions (winding number 3) leading to the annular mode. It then analyzes the two distinct physical scenarios ($\bar{\Gamma}$ vs $\bar{M}$) using effective Hamiltonians and concludes with predictions for candidate materials.
why_interesting: The prediction of a robust, geometrically defined zero-energy state (the ring shape) offers a clear, measurable signature that could be sought in advanced STM experiments on superconducting topological materials, connecting topology to observable quantum phenomena.
